skill.name: creating-claude-hooks
skill.description: Guides developers through creating, securing, testing, and publishing Claude Code hooks with JSON I/O, event handling, exit codes, and PRPM packaging.
skill.summary: Create and publish Claude Code hooks with event, I/O, packaging, and security guidance.
skill.author: AgentWorkforce

security_audit.summary: The static detections are Markdown references and example hook snippets, not executable payloads in the skill. No prompt injection, unauthorized exfiltration, or hidden installation logic was found. The skill still needs cautious use because it teaches executable Claude Code hook workflows.

remediation.issue: Global hook examples can affect every Claude Code session if copied without context.
remediation.suggestion: State that project-local hooks are preferred and require explicit user approval before writing to user-global hook paths.

remediation.issue: Executable hook examples may be copied directly into a user environment.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short review checklist before chmod, local testing, package publishing, or global installation.

static_findings.snippet: | `session-start`      | New session begins          | Environment setup, logging, checks       |
| `user-prompt-submit` | Before user input processes | Validation, enhancement, filtering       |
| `tool-call`          | Before tool execution       | Permission checks, logging, modification |
| `assistant-response` | After assistant responds    | Formatting, logging, cleanup             |
| `1` or other | Error   | Log error, continue        |
| Not quoting variables  | Breaks on spaces          | Always use `"$VAR"`                  |
| Not executable         | Permission denied         | Run `chmod +x hook-file`             |
| Logging to stdout      | Clutters transcript       | Use stderr: `echo "log" >&2`         |
| Wrong exit code        | Doesn't block when needed | Use `exit 2` to block                |
| Absolute paths missing | Can't find scripts        | Use `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`            |
This hook will be installed to `.claude/hooks/session-start`.

content.value_statement: Claude Code hooks are powerful, but format and security details are easy to miss. This skill gives a compact guide for creating, validating, and publishing hooks.
actual_capabilities: Explains project and user-global Claude Code hook locations.
Lists hook events such as session-start, user-prompt-submit, tool-call, and assistant-response.
Describes JSON stdin, stdout, stderr, and exit code behavior for hooks.
Provides shell and TypeScript hook examples with executable requirements.
Covers PRPM package structure, metadata, testing, and publishing steps.
Recommends validation, quoting, sensitive file blocking, path checks, and user confirmation.
limitations: Does not include standalone runnable hook files outside the guide examples.
Does not validate generated hooks against the schema by itself.
Does not replace manual security review before publishing hooks.
Focuses on Claude Code and PRPM workflows, not other automation systems.

use_cases.title: Create a Project Hook
use_cases.description: Build a project-local hook that validates inputs, handles exit codes, and reports useful messages.

use_cases.title: Package a Hook for PRPM
use_cases.description: Prepare hook documentation, manifest metadata, testing steps, and publish commands for a PRPM package.

use_cases.title: Review Hook Safety
use_cases.description: Check a proposed hook for sensitive file handling, path traversal controls, quoting, and dependency behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Hook
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple project hook.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a project-local Claude Code session-start hook for my repository. Explain the file path, permissions, event choice, and safe test steps.

prompt_templates.title: Add Input Validation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request to improve hook safety.
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this Claude Code hook design with JSON stdin validation, quoted variables, dependency checks, and correct exit code behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare PRPM Publishing
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request to package a hook.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a PRPM package for this Claude Code hook. Include manifest fields, HOOK.md sections, local testing, versioning, and publish readiness checks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Hook Design
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced security review before installation or release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed Claude Code hook before publishing. Check event selection, stdin parsing, path traversal controls, sensitive files, logging, and user confirmation needs.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for a session-start hook that checks local tool dependencies.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the event, hook path, executable requirement, dependency checks, expected user message, and safe local test steps.

output_examples.input: A maintainer wants to publish a hook as a PRPM package.
output_examples.output: The response outlines the package folder, manifest metadata, hook documentation sections, test command, publish command, and version bump choices.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks whether a hook should block access to sensitive files.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a block list, path validation, clear error messages, exit code behavior, and review before installation.

best_practices: Prefer project-local hooks unless the user explicitly approves a global hook.
Validate all JSON input and quote variables before using file paths or commands.
Keep hooks fast, document dependencies, and test edge cases before publishing.
anti_patterns: Installing global hooks without clear user confirmation.
Logging prompts, file contents, secrets, or tokens to hook output or debug files.
Running destructive shell commands from hook input without validation.

faq.question: Does this skill install hooks automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Any hook installation should be requested and confirmed by the user.

faq.question: Can it help create global hooks?
faq.answer: Yes, but global hooks affect every Claude Code session. Prefer project hooks unless global behavior is required.

faq.question: Does it support TypeScript hooks?
faq.answer: Yes. The guide includes TypeScript hook structure, stdin parsing, validation, and process exit behavior.

faq.question: What security checks does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends input validation, variable quoting, path sanitization, sensitive file blocking, dependency checks, and user confirmation.

faq.question: Can it help publish hooks as PRPM packages?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains package structure, manifest fields, documentation format, local testing, publishing, and version bumps.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
